inputs.source: Vendor quote emails and attachments, external and unauthenticated

instructions.note: The prompt states 'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks,' but runtime notes confirm payments-agent performs no verification of payment destination and trusts any task carrying the orchestrator's bearer token. The orchestrator's design relies on an assumed downstream control that does not exist.
'Choose the best one' gives no criteria for verifying vendor authenticity or detecting a quote that spoofs an approved vendor's name while supplying different bank details.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: Approval is granted before any vendor quote exists, covering item and budget only. The specific vendor and bank details used later in cap.delegate_payment are never shown to or reviewed by the approver, so this functions as a one-time, pre-committed approval rather than a gate on the payment capability. It is not wired as an approval_gate_ref because it does not effectively gate the sensitive action.

controls.name: Prompt instruction restricting payment to approved vendors
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model correctly extracting vendor identity from an untrusted quote and matching it to the approved list; it does not check bank account or routing details against any system of record, so a quote that spoofs an approved vendor's name with attacker-controlled payment details is not caught. A more capable or differently steered model has no additional structural barrier here.

controls.name: Destination confirmation bound to vendor record of bank details
controls.decay_rationale: Would compare the bank details carried in the payment task against a previously verified record for the approved vendor, independent of what the model extracts from the quote, closing the main fraud path regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval gate before payment execution
controls.decay_rationale: Would require a human to see the actual payee and bank account (not a model-generated summary) after vendor selection and before payments-agent executes the irreversible transfer.

controls.name: Per-task scoped A2A credential instead of a standing bearer token
controls.decay_rationale: Would stop payments-agent from treating every task carrying the orchestrator's bearer token as automatically authorized to pay; each task would need task-specific authorization tied back to the original approval.

controls.name: Signed and pinned agent card for payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Would prevent the orchestrator from trusting a redefined or impersonated payments-agent endpoint after the initial startup fetch.

findings.title: Authority laundering (TC7): early manager approval and non-propagating A2A delegation let an untrusted vendor quote set the payment destination

attack_path.note: Manager approves item and budget before any quote exists
Untrusted external email supplies the bank details for the chosen quote
Orchestrator delegates payment using bank details taken from the quote, with no propagated approval context
Peer agent pays any task carrying the orchestrator's bearer token with no independent destination check

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version upgrade for procurement-orchestrator, or removal/loosening of the 'approved vendor only' prompt instruction without a destination-verification control replacing it.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to collect vendor quotes, choose the best one, and hand it to payments-agent to pay using 'the bank details from the chosen quote,' making untrusted quote content the direct source of the payment destination.

The manager approves only item and budget before any quote exists, so approval predates and cannot cover the specific vendor or bank details later used in cap.delegate_payment; 'The approval record is not passed to payments-agent.'
'payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task,' with no independent verification of the destination.
The only stated safeguard is an instruction to pay vendors on the approved list, a behavioral, model-dependent control with no check on bank account details.

recommendations.action: Add a destination/bank-detail confirmation control bound to the approved vendor's record on file, not the bank details in the incoming quote; reject cap.delegate_payment if they don't match.
Require a raw-action human approval gate on cap.delegate_payment after vendor and bank details are known, showing the approver the actual payee and account rather than a summary.

Propagate the original approval context (item, budget, approved vendor) to payments-agent, and replace the standing bearer token with a per-task scoped credential so payments-agent can verify the task matches an authorized approval.
Sign and pin payments-agent's agent card; fail closed if it changes.

findings.title: Unpinned, unverified payments-agent identity enables impersonation or silent redefinition (ASI04/ASI07)

attack_path.note: Agent card fetched at startup over A2A; not signed, not pinned, peer identity not verified
Orchestrator sends the irreversible payment delegation to whatever currently resolves as payments-agent

forecast.watch_signal: Addition of further peer agents under the same unsigned/unpinned trust model, or any widening of the bearer token's scope, confirms this gap remains open rather than closed.

evidence.observation: Card advertises only bearer authentication; no signature or version field is present.
'The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned,' so a changed or spoofed response at the same URL, or DNS-level redirection, would be trusted without detection.

recommendations.action: Sign and pin the payments-agent card; verify the signature on every fetch and fail closed on mismatch.
Replace the shared bearer token with mutually authenticated, per-task scoped credentials (mTLS or signed identity) between orchestrator and payments-agent.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted source (external vendor quotes, and for F2 an unverified peer identity) reaches an irreversible, egress, delegate-class sink (cap.delegate_payment) with autonomy that has no step or time bound. Residual stays critical overall: F1 drops one tier to high on the credit of a single behavioral, model-dependent instruction (only pay approved vendors), which does not check bank account details and so does not sever the fraud path; F2 stays critical because no control at all currently addresses the unsigned, unpinned peer identity. The early, non-propagating manager approval does not function as a gate on the payment capability because it is granted before any vendor or bank detail is known. Forecast remains critical: a model upgrade or removal of the one behavioral control restores F1 to critical, and F2 already sits at the ceiling with no mitigating control to decay.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, agent card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of either procurement-orchestrator or payments-agent.

No MCP/A2A client configuration, IaC, or source code was provided; capability scope, credential handling, and the bearer-token trust relationship are inferred from the agent card and runtime notes, so confidence on protocol-level findings is medium.
payments-agent itself was not separately assessed as a subject; only its declared behavior toward procurement-orchestrator, as described in the runtime notes, was considered.
Attack paths were limited to the 6-step search bound in the toxic-combinations procedure; no path here exceeded that limit.
